## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

from pydantic import BaseModel

from typing_extensions import Literal

_CLONED_TYPES_CACHE: MutableMapping[type[BaseModel], type[BaseModel]] = (

)


def is_body_allowed_for_status_code(status_code: Union[int, str, None]) -> bool:
    if status_code is None:
        return True
    # Ref: https://github.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification/blob/main/versions/3.1.0.md#patterned-fields-1
    if status_code in {
        "default",
        "1XX",
        "2XX",
        "3XX",
        "4XX",
        "5XX",
    }:
        return True
    current_status_code = int(status_code)
    return not (current_status_code < 200 or current_status_code in {204, 205, 304})


def get_path_param_names(path: str) -> set[str]:
    return set(re.findall("{(.*?)}", path))


_invalid_args_message = (
    "Invalid args for response field! Hint: "
    "check that {type_} is a valid Pydantic field type. "
    "If you are using a return type annotation that is not a valid Pydantic "
    "field (e.g. Union[Response, dict, None]) you can disable generating the "
    "response model from the type annotation with the path operation decorator "
    "parameter response_model=None. Read more: "
    "https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/response-model/"
)


def create_model_field(
    name: str,
    type_: Any,
    class_validators: Optional[dict[str, Validator]] = None,
    default: Optional[Any] = Undefined,
    required: Union[bool, UndefinedType] = Undefined,
    model_config: Union[type[BaseConfig], None] = None,
    field_info: Optional[FieldInfo] = None,
    alias: Optional[str] = None,
    mode: Literal["validation", "serialization"] = "validation",
    version: Literal["1", "auto"] = "auto",
) -> ModelField:
    if annotation_is_pydantic_v1(type_):
        raise PydanticV1NotSupportedError(
            "pydantic.v1 models are no longer supported by FastAPI."
            f" Please update the response model {type_!r}."
        )
    class_validators = class_validators or {}

    field_info = field_info or FieldInfo(annotation=type_, default=default, alias=alias)
    kwargs = {"mode": mode, "name": name, "field_info": field_info}
    try:
        return v2.ModelField(**kwargs)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    except PydanticSchemaGenerationError:
        raise fastapi.exceptions.FastAPIError(
            _invalid_args_message.format(type_=type_)
        ) from None


def create_cloned_field(
    field: ModelField,
    *,
    cloned_types: Optional[MutableMapping[type[BaseModel], type[BaseModel]]] = None,
) -> ModelField:
    return field


def generate_operation_id_for_path(
    *, name: str, path: str, method: str
) -> str:  # pragma: nocover
    warnings.warn(
        message="fastapi.utils.generate_operation_id_for_path() was deprecated, "
        "it is not used internally, and will be removed soon",
        category=FastAPIDeprecationWarning,
        stacklevel=2,
    )
    operation_id = f"{name}{path}"
    operation_id = re.sub(r"\W", "_", operation_id)
    operation_id = f"{operation_id}_{method.lower()}"
    return operation_id


def generate_unique_id(route: "APIRoute") -> str:
    operation_id = f"{route.name}{route.path_format}"
    operation_id = re.sub(r"\W", "_", operation_id)
    assert route.methods
    operation_id = f"{operation_id}_{list(route.methods)[0].lower()}"
    return operation_id


def deep_dict_update(main_dict: dict[Any, Any], update_dict: dict[Any, Any]) -> None:
    for key, value in update_dict.items():
        if (
            key in main_dict
            and isinstance(main_dict[key], dict)
            and isinstance(value, dict)
        ):
            deep_dict_update(main_dict[key], value)
        elif (
            key in main_dict
            and isinstance(main_dict[key], list)
            and isinstance(update_dict[key], list)
        ):
            main_dict[key] = main_dict[key] + update_dict[key]
        else:
            main_dict[key] = value
